headline_item.title_zh: Embo融资1.1亿美元研发具身智能世界模型
headline_item.title_en: Embo, which is developing world models for robotics trained on massive amounts of internet video, emerges from stealth with a $110M seed led by a16z (Embo)
headline_item.author: Embo
headline_item.event_summary_zh: Embo宣布完成1.1亿美元种子轮融资，由a16z领投，旨在通过互联网规模视频预训练开发具备物理理解能力的机器人世界模型
headline_item.event_summary_en: Embodied AI startup Embo secured $110 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz to develop unified robot 'brains' using internet-scale video pretraining. Composed of talent from Google DeepMind, Meta, and NVIDIA, the team aims to build world models capable of physical reasoning and high-frequency motor control to solve generalization limitations in robotics.
core_facts_zh: 【核心事件】Embo（机器人AI初创公司），Andreessen Horowitz（领投方）在机器人具身智能研发领域：完成1.1亿美元种子轮融资，构建基于视频预训练的通用机器人世界模型
【起因与机理】旨在解决现有机器人对陌生场景泛化能力差、技能脆弱且难以部署的问题
【关键数据与实测】获得1.1亿美元种子轮融资，由a16z领投。
【各方立场与态度】目标是解决现有机器人在陌生场景下的动作泛化与鲁棒性挑战。
core_facts_en: [Core Event] Embo, Andreessen Horowitz (Embodied AI R&D sector): Raised $110M seed round to develop general-purpose world models for robots
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To address fragility and poor generalization of current robots in unfamiliar environments
[Key Metrics] Secured $110M seed funding led by a16z.
[Key Position & Outlook] Focusing on overcoming robot generalization and robustness issues in unfamiliar scenarios.
headline_item.industry_impact_zh: 机器人领域的“缩放定律”正从文本转向物理视频空间，Embo通过预训练解决电机控制与视觉密度不匹配的问题，这是具身智能能否从实验室走向规模化部署的关键阈值。该领域未来竞争焦点将从算法模型迅速转移至高质量机器人实时体验数据的闭环采集能力，谁拥有垂直领域的硬件 fleet，谁就掌握了通往通用人形机器人的核心护城河。
headline_item.industry_impact_en: The scaling laws in robotics are pivoting from text to physical video space. Embo's approach to reconciling motor control density with visual data is the critical threshold for scalable deployment. Future competition will shift from purely algorithmic models to the closed-loop acquisition of proprietary, high-quality robotics experience data.

headlines.title_zh: 美国MATCH法案拟禁ASML对华设备服务
headlines.title_en: How the MATCH Act could backfire by barring ASML from its ~350 immersion scanners in China, letting rivals service and reverse engineer them, and hire its staff (LithoWar)
headlines.author: LithoWar
headlines.event_summary_zh: MATCH法案拟禁止ASML在中国提供光刻机售后服务，或引发逆向工程风险与人才流失
headlines.event_summary_en: The proposed MATCH Act seeks to prohibit ASML from providing maintenance and technical support for approximately 350 immersion scanners currently in China. This move aims to further restrict China's advanced chip manufacturing capabilities but risks allowing local competitors to provide service, potentially facilitating reverse engineering of critical processes and the poaching of ASML technical staff.
core_facts_zh: 【核心事件】阿斯麦（ASML）、美国立法机构在美国及中国半导体制造领域：禁止ASML为中国存量浸没式光刻机提供售后服务
【起因与机理】通过阻断技术生命周期支持，遏制中国先进工艺节点的迭代
【关键数据与实测】法案旨在切断ASML在华约350台浸没式光刻机的维护支持。
【行业影响与走向】该法案可能削弱跨国设备厂商的市场控制力并倒逼国产设备服务链加速成熟。
core_facts_en: [Core Event] ASML, U.S. Legislative bodies: Prohibit ASML from providing maintenance for existing immersion scanners in China
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To stifle China's advanced process node iteration by cutting off life-cycle technical support
[Key Fact Detail] Proposed ban on maintenance services for 350+ ASML scanners in China.
[Key Position & Outlook] Potential acceleration of China's localized service ecosystem and loss of influence for Western vendors.
headlines.industry_impact_zh: 该法案的激进之处在于试图通过切断售后支持实现物理层面的设备淘汰，但其产业反噬效应显著。此举不仅会加速中国国产光刻机配套服务体系的自主闭环，还将迫使ASML流失在该地区的深度工艺调试人才，最终损害西方设备厂商对全球技术生态的掌控力。
headlines.industry_impact_en: The radical aspect of this act is the attempt to force hardware obsolescence by severing maintenance, yet the industrial backfire is inevitable. It will accelerate the self-reliance of China's localized lithography service ecosystem while causing ASML to lose deep process-tuning talent, ultimately undermining Western equipment manufacturers' grip on the global technology stack.

谷歌有一个新的 tibo，就像 neon 是世界上最热门的前沿模型一样诞生。银行重置和所有

这是一个完全焕发活力的 GDM，与我记忆中的 Gemini 2.5 以来我们从未见过它不同。 @latentspacepod 即将发表文章，但基本上自 2023 年以来，前沿和近前沿实验室的数量每年都增加一倍，这是迄今为止最大的存在，反驳了惨痛的教训是人工智能产业经济的唯一决定因素。 @saranormous 称之为神经多样性模型，基本上它是驱动特工实验室和人工智能工程生死存亡的最重要的宏观因素。
celebrity.quote_en:
google has a new tibo, spawning just as neon is the hottest frontier model in the world. banked resets and all

this is a completely revitalized GDM unlike which we have not seen since basically Gemini 2.5 in my memory. writeup coming @latentspacepod but basically the # of frontier and near-frontier labs has ~doubled every year since 2023 and that’s by far the biggest existence disproof that the bitter lesson is the sole determinant of ai industrial economics. @saranormous calls it model neurodiversity and basically its the single most impt macro factor driving the life/death of agent labs and ai engineering.

titans.name: @omarsar0
titans.event_context_zh:
人工智能并不会让团队变得更聪明。

如果您尝试构建代理群，这一点尤其重要。

这项工作特别询问代理团队是否可以在相同的计算预算下递归地改进。

他们检查这种收益是来自团队合作还是来自额外的计算。一个团队使用的代币比一个代理要多得多。以相同的代币预算自行运行多个代理并获得多数票已经解释了大部分收益。

因此，作者在相同的计算下针对三个条形图对每个团队进行了测试。该团队必须击败一名特工。然后它必须击败独立代理人的多数票。最难的栏是一组独立的代理，如果其中任何一个人做对了，任务就被视为已解决。

只有当每个特工掌握不同的事实并将其传递给其他特工时，团队合作才能克服最困难的障碍。在该设置中，团队以三种模型尺寸击败了最难的标准，其中 27B 模型的领先优势约为三分之一。

由相同的 27B 特工组成的团队也会在没有被告知的情况下自行组织起来。一些代理成为收集和共享信息的中心，准确率提高了 18 个点。

然后，各小组根据自己经过验证的输出（没有标签）来训练下一代。在 PlanBench、HiddenBench 和 Hanabi 上，每一代在四到六代中都在未见过的问题上击败了前一代。

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32606

与 Paper 聊天：https://academy.dair.ai/papers/recursive-collective-intelligence-emergence-on-an-equal-budget-ladder-in-multi-a-2611.32606

titans.quote_en:
Must-read paper on recursive collective intelligence.

Highly recommend if you are planning to use agent swarms.

They find that an agent team beats AIs working alone only when each one knows something the others don't and shares it.

This aligns with my suspicion that collective intelligence comes from pooling different knowledge. Adding more AIs that all know the same things doesn't make the group smarter.

This is particularly important if you are trying to build agent swarms.

This work specifically asks if agent teams can improve recursively at the same compute budget.

They check whether that gain comes from teamwork or from extra compute. A team uses many more tokens than one agent. Running several agents on their own with the same token budget and taking a majority vote already explains most of the gain.

So the authors test each team against three bars, all at the same compute. The team has to beat one agent. Then it has to beat a majority vote of independent agents. The hardest bar is a group of independent agents where a task counts as solved if any one of them gets it right.

Teamwork cleared the hardest bar only when each agent held different facts and passed them on to the others. In that setup, teams beat the hardest bar at three model sizes, by about a third with 27B models.

Teams of identical 27B agents also organized themselves without being told to. A few agents became hubs that collected and shared information, and accuracy rose 18 points.

Groups then trained their next generation on their own verified outputs, with no labels. On PlanBench, HiddenBench, and Hanabi, each generation beat the previous one on unseen problems for four to six generations.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32606

Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/recursive-collective-intelligence-emergence-on-an-equal-budget-ladder-in-multi-a-2611.32606
